requires.label: Cooperation required for financial assistance
requires.quote: Applicants for financial assistance are responsible for applying for public programs for available coverage. They are expected to pursue public or private health insurance coverage for care by Intermountain health. The patient’s, or a patient’s guarantor’s, cooperation in applying for applicable programs and identifiable funding sources, including COBRA coverage (a federal law allowing for a time-limited extension of health care benefits) shall be required.

requires.label: Residency required for non-emergent services
requires.quote: Residency within an Intermountain service area for non-emergent hospital services and/or extenuating circumstances. Trauma and emergency services provided in an emergency setting are covered regardless of residency status.

rules.label: Fully Discounted (No Charge) Care
rules.quote: Uninsured and Underinsured patients meeting other eligibility criteria and with annual family incomes not in excess of 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines

rules.label: Discounted Care
rules.quote: Uninsured and underinsured patients meeting other eligibility criteria and whose annualized family incomes are in excess of 250% but less than or equal to 500% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines

payment_plan.quote: A reasonable payment plan will be established between Intermountain Health and the patient, or patient guarantor, for any balance remaining after the cost of care has been discounted under the financial assistance policy.

notes: The policy references a Financial Assistance Patient Responsibility Matrix – Attachment B for discount percentages in the Discounted Care tier, but specific percentages are not detailed in the provided text.
The policy mentions that Financial Assistance will be applied to all eligible accounts incurred for services received prior to application date.

The policy states that Intermountain Health will not charge patients eligible for Financial Assistance under this policy for emergency or other Medically Necessary care more than the AGB to individuals who have insurance.
The policy defines Medically Necessary as services or items reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury, as defined by Medicare.
The policy specifies that Intermountain Health updates its federal poverty table annually on April 1st.

The policy lists exclusions: Elective procedures not Medically Necessary including cosmetic services, and other care providers not billed through Intermountain Health (e.g., independent physician services, private-duty nursing, ambulance transport, etc.).
The policy states that Financial Assistance determinations will be made after all efforts to qualify the patient for other public or private programs have been exhausted.
The policy requires that patients apply for public programs for available coverage and pursue public or private health insurance coverage.

The policy states that Information on Financial Assistance policies or programs is readily available and posted on all Intermountain Health websites and conspicuously posted in emergency departments, urgent care centers, admitting and registration areas.
The policy mentions that Financial Assistance information, including a contact number, shall be included in patient bills and through oral communication.
